session_title: First Question of the New Year: In the AI Era, How Should We Develop Our Skill Tree?

content.text: Happy New Year! I just read an in-depth analysis about the impact of AI on the programming and content industries in 2025, and I forwarded it to you. Have you seen it? It feels like AI-assisted programming is getting stronger and stronger—do you think basic programmers like us might lose our jobs? And for those of you in content creation, AI-generated content is pretty impressive too. Coincidentally, during our New Year's Eve gaming session yesterday, we were talking about the projects we collaborated on this year, from the health dashboard to the animal adoption platform. Technology keeps changing, but our collaboration model seems to be getting more and more solid.

Happy New Year! I just read it too. I think it's more about the evolution of tools rather than the extinction of professions. Just like how photography didn't kill painting but instead gave rise to new artistic styles. For us, it might mean focusing more on areas where AI isn't as strong: your architectural design, breaking down complex problems, and understanding the business; my in-depth interviews, unique perspectives, emotional resonance, and interpersonal relationships. This New Year, we should think about how to make AI our "co-pilot" rather than our "replacement." It reminds me of when we worked on the health dashboard project—the technical tools were just aids, and the core was still about changing human habits and social accountability.

Well said! Just like when we were working on the health dashboard earlier, AI could help generate code snippets, but the overall architecture and business logic still had to be managed by us. By the way, I’ve been optimizing the campus information aggregator recently, using AI to process unstructured information, which has significantly improved efficiency. However, the core requirement analysis still relies on people—just like when we discussed information anxiety in October, the user scenarios you defined, AI can’t understand the pain of that FOMO.

I've compiled a table outlining the implementation path for AI as a 'co-pilot.' Look, this summarizes the application scenarios and substitution boundaries across different career directions. For example, for you, writing business code in the future might become a fundamental skill, much like writing SQL is today, but AI still can't handle complex system design. The design approach for this table actually draws inspiration from the 'technology-experience' dual-perspective report we created during our review of the digital art exhibition, clearly distinguishing the core value of tools and humans.

Wow, this table is amazing! Just like we discussed when doing sentiment analysis before, AI can crawl data and perform sentiment analysis, but ethical boundaries and business insights still rely on humans. Let me see, it mentions 'core actions' here—indeed, my skill tree needs to focus on architecture and business understanding. This reminds me of the results we compared during the annual review. No matter how dense my GitHub commit history is, if I lack a deep understanding of the problems, I could easily be replaced by AI.

Exactly! For me, AI can mimic styles, but it struggles to replicate unique personal experiences and the depth of thought. Like that digital art exhibition—you explained the technology, while I documented the experience. AI could generate a report, but the on-site interaction and emotional resonance were one-of-a-kind. This New Year, we need to "harness" AI together, not "fear" it. Just like when we set off fireworks on the mountaintop in the game at midnight—behind the dazzling virtual code lies our real friendship and collaborative memories.

Forwarding an image to you—the interaction between the robot hand and the human hand reminds me of our collaborative projects. From health dashboards to animal adoption platforms, technology is merely a tool; the core lies in human creativity and collaboration. In the AI era, our skill sets may need to focus more on these "soft skills." Just like the mini-program we developed for stray animals on campus, the technical implementation can be open-source, but it’s the heartwarming animal "profiles" and promotional strategies that truly resonate with people.

This image is so vivid! It's like in a cooperative game: you analyze the mechanics, I observe the social dynamics, and AI can assist, but teamwork and real-time reactions are things machines can't learn. By the way, speaking of skill trees, how did your internship season go with buying a new computer? With AI assistance, is the choice of productivity tools even more crucial now? I remember when you were comparing screen sizes and configurations, you even used our health dashboard's data-driven decision-making framework.

Haha, thanks to your previous advice on rational consumption, I calculated the time cost and decided not to upgrade for now. Instead, I’ll optimize my workflow using existing equipment and AI tools. As shown in the annual report of the health dashboard, data-driven decision-making is crucial. AI can help me write code, but hardware investments still depend on actual needs. Moreover, the server for our newly launched animal adoption platform is running smoothly, proving that the current equipment can still handle the load. Under the spirit of open-source sharing, efficiency doesn’t necessarily rely on the latest hardware.

Wise! It's just like our campus cat catalog project—the technical implementation can be accelerated by AI, but the warm descriptions of the animals' "resumes" and the promotion strategies still rely on human touch. In the new year, I plan to practice more in-depth interviews, letting AI handle the audio-to-text conversion while I focus on emotional exploration—just like how we discussed in sentiment analysis how to go beyond the data and understand the emotional spread behind the topics.

Great idea! I can help you develop an AI-assisted tool to optimize the interview process. Just like the information aggregator project, when we combine technology and communication, the impact multiplies. In the AI era, cross-disciplinary collaboration might be even more important—you handle the "human" side, and I'll take care of the "machine" side. This is essentially an upgraded version of our collaboration model over the past year: from tech geeks intervening in health crises, to observers in gaming field research, and now to technical communication partners for public welfare projects.

Completely agree! This reminds me of our year-end project review, where we appreciated each other's professional skills. AI might change the way we work, but our collaboration model—tech enthusiast plus social expert—becomes even more valuable. Let's level up our skills together in the new year, with AI as our co-pilot, and soar to new heights! Just like we said at the end of the New Year's Eve game night, I'm so grateful to have a friend like you who can work on projects together, have fun together, and now, "face technological changes together."

Well said! Just like a New Year's Eve gaming session, we can have fun and grow together. AI is both a challenge and an opportunity. I plan to learn more about system architecture and business analysis this year. How about you? Do you have any specific goals? We can set phased objectives, just like the health dashboard project, and track progress with data.

I want to enhance my data storytelling skills by combining my experience in public opinion analysis and using AI visualization tools to tell compelling stories. Just like a health dashboard, behind the data lies changes in people's habits. With the assistance of AI, I can more efficiently uncover unique perspectives. By the way, in the sustainable health habit solutions we just discussed, aren’t there multiple dimensions such as technology, social interaction, and goal setting? Developing skills in the AI era also requires such a multi-dimensional approach.

Excellent! We can continue our collaboration, such as using AI to analyze data from the animal adoption platform and optimizing the matching algorithm. At the beginning of the new year, starting a growth dialogue with this kind of intellectual resonance makes the future feel full of possibilities. Let's work together, harness AI, and avoid being replaced! Just like how we find homes for the "cat seniors," the combination of technology and human warmth is truly irreplaceable.

Yes! From health crises to the AI era, we have always been great partners. The first answer of the new year is: skill up and let technology serve humanity. Looking forward to more project collaborations this year, continuous intellectual resonance, and facing future challenges together! Let’s keep our health dashboard points motivating and maintain this cross-disciplinary friendship synergy. We’ll review it all again next New Year’s Eve!
